annotationRationale: The primary method compares central-triangle decompositions using a common radius. The alternative uses an enclosing square, subtraction, and the Pythagorean theorem, providing a complete route without trigonometry. Both depend on regular-polygon structure and area decomposition.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Geometry is correct. No subject repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: With circumradius R, the octagon has area 2√2 R² and the alternating-vertex square has area 2R². Their ratio is √2/2, choice B. The stem, choices and key agree; the constructions can be followed without a supplied figure.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: The LIVE circumradius route is retained, and AoPS Solution 3 (Deriving Formulas) is retained through the simplified enclosing-square construction. AoPS's other area-formula and apothem calculations add no necessary route beyond these complete trigonometric and nontrigonometric solutions. AoPS Solution 5's shared-altitude ratio is an equivalent simplification of central-triangle comparison. No shared-bank methods were supplied.
review.annotationCheck: Regular-polygon structure and area decomposition are appropriate assessed concepts. Triangle area and square properties support both methods; special-angle evaluation and the Pythagorean theorem are correctly confined to their respective routes.
review.areaCheck: Geometry is correct. No subject repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Each octagon sector has area R² sin(45°)/2, so eight sectors total 2√2 R². Alternate vertices have 90° central spacing, and their square consists of four right triangles of area R²/2. The common positive R² cancels to give √2/2.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The LIVE attribution accurately identifies the common-circumradius argument. The candidate derives both area values in its own explanatory sequence rather than merely repeating the reference's formulas. The nonofficial source classification and reference ID are correct.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The common-radius motivation explains the first move. The central angles, altitude, congruent triangle counts and square identification are all justified.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: Regular polygons and circles, composite area, triangle area, special-angle values and square properties all directly support the written calculations.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: All supplied exact native links match the regular-polygon, area, square and special-angle concepts used.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: 6.G.A.1 directly supports the decomposition. The other area links cover limited components; rectilinear-only 3.MD.C.7d does not describe this triangular partition. G-CO.A.3 offers a symmetry connection, while no inscribed construction under G-CO.D.13 is performed. F-TF.A.3 is partial special-angle use, and the square hierarchy links are supporting only.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: The nodes are precise and sufficient for the central-triangle method; no memorized polygon-area formula is assumed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The removed corners are right isosceles triangles with leg t=s/√2, and the enclosing square has side s+2t. Subtraction gives n=(2+2√2)s². At the specified corner T, AT=s+t and TC=t are perpendicular, giving AC²=(2+√2)s². Since ACEG is a square, the resulting ratio is √2/2.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: AoPS Solution 3 (Deriving Formulas) is the correct source for the enclosure idea. The candidate gives an independent, shorter calculation of AC and correctly uses s+2t, avoiding the archived source's erroneous enclosing-side formula. The third-party basis and credit are accurate.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The named extended sides and corner T locate every necessary segment. The two Pythagorean calculations and area subtraction are explicit enough to reconstruct without a new diagram.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: The regular-polygon, composite-area, triangle-area, Pythagorean and square-property nodes all occur directly. Their scopes cover the construction without requiring trigonometry.
